title: Static electricity by rubbing (ঘর্ষণে স্থির বিদ্যুৎ)
placement: Book page 274, topic 10.2 ঘর্ষণে স্থির বিদ্যুৎ তৈরি, চিত্র ১০.০২ and ১০.০৩ (pp. 274–275).
description: Charging by rubbing and like and unlike charges (pages 274–275, topic 10.2, চিত্র ১০.০২ and ১০.০৩). On a plain sand table in a calm deep-blue setting: a clear glass rod and a piece of silk, a plastic rod and a piece of flannel, each rod on two wooden V-blocks with the cloth draped over its end; behind them two lab stands, each with a rod hanging from a silk thread tied at its middle. Charges are signs that face the camera (red + protons, blue − electrons, the sign always drawn). Every body starts neutral; rubbing (a tap, or dragging the cloth back and forth, with a count of strokes) moves electrons only: three hop from the glass to the silk, and from the flannel to the plastic. Then the book's experiment: the rubbed rod is held near a hanging one (a tap, or dragging the rod) and the hanging rod turns away (+ and +, − and −) or toward it (+ and −), from a Coulomb torque about the thread, with outlined teal force arrows on both rods. Five experiments in the book's order, each in two steps (look, then do); a row of what has been found; the book's rule. Test: five tap questions (which way electrons move, the flannel's charge read off its signs, predict the swing, a hanging rod's unknown charge, why two kinds of force). Phone-first, Bangla and English.
